approver: owner, who on 2026-11-17 changed the revision rule so a grading change moves the published revision, and chose to bump OME-1907's 47 revisions in this PR together with the re-grade (OME-1909)
scope: Prior-test edits in eleven files and nothing else, pinned against main at d4848c55d (this branch's merge base with main, after #1783 and #1892 landed). (1) test_published_revisions.py: 47 literals move to the new published ids, each with a comment naming its old id, and one header line says why. (2) test_benchmark_fingerprints.py: the docstring and failure message state the 2026-11-17 rule, and the OME-1907 comment now says the ids moved instead of held; no fingerprint literal moves. (3) test_benchmark_foundation.py: the exact catalogue entry gains "regradable_from": [], with a comment. (4) test_leaderboard_routes.py: regraded_from_id and regraded_by join the internal set of test_every_score_field_reaches_at_least_one_read_dto. (5) public_surface_snapshot.json: regenerated with UPDATE_SURFACE_SNAPSHOT=1; only Client.regrade, AsyncClient.regrade, LeaderboardError's existing_score_id and LeaderboardScore's regraded_from move. (6) _fakes.py, test_queue_admission.py, test_answer_seed_threading.py, test_cache_policy_threading.py, test_e2e_compose_flow.py and test_run_control_resilience.py: each job-runner fake's schedule() gains one keyword parameter, replay_live_judge: LiveJudge | None = None, after replay_frozen_copy, and its job_env import adds LiveJudge. Nothing else in those files moves.
reason: (1) The published ids move because the 2026-11-17 rule moves the id on a grading change, and OME-1907 changed how these 47 rows grade a wrapped answer letter. (2) The fingerprint pins state the rule a red literal points to, and that rule changed. (3) Every catalogue entry now carries regradable_from (empty when a Benchmark declares none), so the exact-equality entry must name it. (4) The Score table gains the re-grade link, published as regraded_from, and the re-grader's email, stored for audit and deliberately on no read schema. (5) The SDK's public surface gains the re-grade call, the 409's existing re-grade id and a score's re-grade link, and the snapshot exists to record exactly such a change. (6) The job runner port's schedule() gained replay_live_judge (the re-grade's live judge Cases), and pyright refuses an override that drops a parameter of the method it overrides (reportIncompatibleMethodOverride). Each fake accepts it exactly as the port declares it, as these fakes already do for capture and replay_frozen_copy.
